findings.finding: Upper treads inside the arch are all about the same height as the lower ones, so the rise into the doorway reads flat; at 1x the top two lit treads merge into a single pale band.
findings.fix: Shrink the top two tread+riser pairs to 2px+1px (vs 3px+2px lower) and put one dark 1px riser line between the two lit treads.

findings.finding: The brass runner rods barely show against the red runner at 1x, so the runner reads as a flat red stripe.
findings.fix: Put a 1px brass highlight pixel at each rod end where it meets the stone tread, on every tread.

findings.finding: It reads as a stone fireplace or hearth seen from the front, not as a hole in the floor. The north inner wall is a dark grid of block shapes like a firebox back wall. The trapezoid inner walls look like angled firebox cheeks. The north rail is a thick light bar that reads as a mantel. At 1x beside the student it looks like an upright framed opening, not a floor opening.
findings.fix: Replace the block-grid north inner wall with 1-2 rows of flat darkest-value fill (no mortar grid). Drop the north rail cap to 2px, mid-value, with a 1px floor shadow below its south edge only. Let the room floor's flagstone pattern continue right up to the outside of the rails on all three sides so the piece reads as cut into the floor. Make each tread nosing a full-width 1px light line, so the treads read as horizontal planes rather than stacked bricks.

findings.finding: The south (entry) tread is noticeably lighter than the surrounding floor and boxed by the side rails, so it reads as a raised sill rather than being level with the floor.
findings.fix: Set the first tread to the floor's mid flagstone value and end the side rails 2px short of the south edge.

findings.finding: The oak faces are large orange bands with only a thin light top edge, so tread and riser are ambiguous; in the place at 3x it can read as a set of wooden shelves or drawers inside an iron frame.
findings.fix: Make each tread top 2-3px of the light oak value and each riser 1-2px of the dark oak value, so the light tops are bigger than the dark fronts. Add a 1px darkest shadow line under each nosing.

findings.finding: Same tread/riser ambiguity as the clock stair: between two bookcases the oak steps can read as a chest of drawers in an arch. The warm light at the top is a single yellow cap rather than light spilling down the top treads.
findings.fix: Lighten the top 2 tread tops toward the warm yellow and shorten their risers. Use 2px light tops over 1px dark risers on the lower treads.

findings.finding: Stacked boxes sit directly south of the entrance cell. Walking straight in from the south is blocked visually, though the stair is still reachable from the west.
findings.fix: Move the crate stack one cell east or west so the cell directly south of the stair entrance is clear floor.

findings.finding: The straw and dropping specks are scattered over several treads and read as noise or damage at 1x rather than as details.
findings.fix: Keep one 2-3px straw tuft on one lower tread and the single dropping; remove the other specks.

findings.finding: Same problem as the castle stairwell, and it ships in the owlery. With a full wooden frame on north/west/east and a block-grid dark back, it reads at 3x as a wooden-framed oven or fireplace standing against the floor, not a stairwell you walk down into.
findings.fix: Same fix as wz-castle-stair-down. Make the wooden rails 2px caps with a 1px floor shadow. Use a flat dark north inner wall with no mortar grid, and continue the floor pattern right up to the rails. Make the treads read as planes with full-width light nosings. Keep the feather on the south tread.

places.finding: Owlery: the stairwell sits hard against the west wall border, so its west rail is visually absorbed into the wall trim. That adds to the framed-opening read.
places.fix: Shift it one cell east, or drop the west rail cap 1px lower in value than the wall trim, so the rail separates from the wall.

places.finding: Honeydukes: the crate stack south of the stair entrance crowds the walk-in cell.
places.fix: Move the crates one cell aside.
